kind: search plan as stated (Airy's Suggestions of 13 July 1846 as Challis reports them)
zone_ra: centre 325° of longitude on the ecliptic, 15° of longitude each way (30° long); RA extent marked out for each 1° declination interval
zone_dec: 5° of latitude north and south (10° broad) in 1° intervals; zone breadth 15′ at power 120; NPD estimated from horizontal wires 3′ apart
depth_magnitude: magnitudes always to be noted (no limit stated)
duration: 80 zones averaging one hour; 3 sweeps at least, each finished before the next; 300 hours
sources: Challis Memoirs 16, 416–417; MNRAS 7, 145; Airy MNRAS 7, 136 (30° by 10°)
notes: The Suggestions themselves are in the Airy papers (RGO 6/96a) and are not in print; Airy's note proposing the search is dated 9 July.

method: first sweep telescope fixed, second telescope moving (clock drive, hour-circle read), third if needed; sector sweeps of 80′ in NPD for reference stars
zone_dec: zone breadth 9′ at power 166; declination read on the micrometer comb (one revolution 17″, parts to a fourth, error ≤ 4″)
depth_magnitude: all stars visible with the field illuminated: 11th magnitude included (Adams's 9th-magnitude inference, received in conversation, not adopted)
comparison: comparison of the fixed and moving series meant to reveal the planet as a star in the second not in the first
sources: Challis Memoirs 16, 417–421; MNRAS 7, 145–146; Challis to Airy 12 Oct 1846 (power 160)
notes: Power 166 in the Memoirs and abstract, 160 in the 12 October letter. Moonlight: fixed telescope only. Clouds: clock set going and a line drawn in the memorandum-book.

zone_ra: "the part of the heavens which theory had indicated as the most probable position": Adams's 325° place (21h 50.5m, −13° 4′ interpolated)
zone_dec: declination-rod reading the same as on July 30 and August 4; breadth not stated
neptune_in_zone: not determinable: the zone's RA extent is not printed. Neptune was 8.3 min of time east and 10′ north of Adams's 325° place; a 9′ zone centred on that place excludes it, but the zone's actual declination is not printed

zone_ra: not stated; the August 12 zone "exceeded in length that of July 30, but included the whole of it"
zone_dec: zone of 9′ breadth; same declination-rod reading as July 29 and August 4
depth_magnitude: 11th magnitude (""sure that none brighter than the 11th escaped me"")
neptune_in_zone: outside (primary): the planet "had wandered into the zone in the interval between July 30 and August 12" (Memoirs 424; letter). Which edge it crossed (RA end or declination edge) is not printed; it moved 1m 18s west and 7′ south between the two nights

method: sector: telescope moved in declination by the milled head, polar axis fixed
planet_recorded: yes: 21h 58m 14.70s, NPD 102° 57′ 32.2″ at 13h 36m 25s GMT (reduced after the discovery)
notes: Declination read on the sector microscope micrometer (one revolution 10″, parts to a fourth, error ≤ 3″). Challis's place agrees with the computed apparent place to 0.3 s and 4″.

zone_ra: greater extent in RA than July 30, including the whole of it; direction of the extension not stated
zone_dec: zone 9′ broad in the same position as July 30
planet_recorded: yes: 21h 57m 26.13s, NPD 103° 2′ 0.2″ at 13h 3m 26s GMT (No. 49 of the series; parts of a revolution estimated to a tenth)
notes: Moonlight and weather prevented observing between August 4 and 12. Challis's place agrees with the computed apparent place to 0.2 s and 2″.

date_1846: August 13 ("probably the next day"; no memorandum)
kind: comparison of the July 30 and August 12 series
comparison: every star to No. 39 of the August 12 (fixed) series found in the July 30 (moving) series; stopped at the line drawn when a cloud interrupted; No. 49, a star of the 8th magnitude, would have been found wanting
sources: Memoirs 16, 422, 424; MNRAS 7, 147–148; letter of 12 Oct ("within a very few stars of the planet")
notes: Purpose stated: to test the efficiency of the moving-telescope method, not to find the planet.

method: principally telescope fixed; the ground partly gone over again telescope moving
zone_ra: "earlier in right ascension" than the planet (letter: "too early in right ascension")
star_count: "some thousands" (letter); the total of all sessions above 3000
duration: two months at all available opportunities
planet_recorded: no (""did not again fall in with the planet"")
neptune_in_zone: outside (primary: the zones were east of the planet in RA; their limits are not printed)
sources: Memoirs 16, 422; MNRAS 7, 147; letters of 2 Sept and 12 Oct
notes: "Earlier in right ascension" means smaller RA, i.e. west of the planet, which was moving west at ~6 s per day.

kind: session (plan changed after reading Le Verrier's 31 August paper)
method: sweep over "a considerable breadth in declination" within Le Verrier's limits of longitude; physical appearance of the brighter stars noted
zone_ra: within the limits of longitude marked out by Le Verrier (not printed by Challis)
zone_dec: a considerable breadth in declination (not quantified)
depth_magnitude: 11th magnitude kept; brighter stars examined for a disk
duration: three hours and a half without intermission
planet_recorded: yes: one star noted "It seems to have a disk"; place 21h 52m 48.9s, NPD 103° 26′ 30″ at 10h 10m GMT from B.A.C. 7599
notes: Challis's rough place agrees with the computed apparent place to 0.3 s and 8″. Night was good.
"the moon being in the way" (Memoirs); "could not be repeated the next night" (abstract).
News of Galle's discovery of September 23 received.

zone_dec: "but a small portion of the space intended to be explored"
depth_magnitude: for the most part stars of very small magnitude
notes: Preparations for mapping the stars made, not carried out.
